About Bain Capital Specialty Finance, Inc. Bain Capital Specialty Finance, Inc. is an externally managed specialty finance company focused on lending to middle market companies. BCSF is managed by BCSF Advisors, LP, an SEC-registered investment adviser and a subsidiary of Bain Capital Credit, LP. Since commencing investment operations on October 13, 2016, and through September 30, 2026, BCSF has invested approximately $10,238.4 million in aggregate principal amount of debt and equity investments prior to any subsequent exits or repayments. BCSF’s investment objective is to generate current income and, to a lesser extent, capital appreciation through direct originations of secured debt, including first lien, first lien/last out, unitranche and second lien debt, investments in strategic joint ventures, equity investments and, to a lesser extent, corporate bonds. BCSF has elected to be regulated as a business development company under the Investment Company Act of 1940, as amended. articles.summary: CECO Environmental Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results Matthew.Callan… Mon, 11/09/2026 - 07:00 CECO Environmental Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results November 9, 2026 General Record Third Quarter Results Highlighted by Orders, Backlog and Adjusted EBITDA, Each Up Over 200 Percent Company Updates 2026 Outlook, Increasing Full Year Orders and Free Cash Flow Forecast Company Introduces Full Year 2027 Outlook ADDISON, Texas, Nov. 09, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- CECO Environmental Corp. (TXSE: CECO) ("CECO," or the “Company”) , a leading environmentally focused, diversified industrial company whose solutions protect people, the environment, and industrial equipment, today reported its financial results for the third quarter of 2026. Highlights for the Quarter (1) Third quarter as a combined company following the June 1, 2026 acquisition of Thermon Orders of $777.6 million, up 234 percent; backlog of $2,193.5 million, up 205 percent Revenue of $404.4 million, up 105 percent Gross profit of $130.1 million, up 101 percent; gross margin of 32.2 percent; Non-GAAP gross profit of $146.8 million, up 127 percent; non-GAAP gross margin of 36.3 percent Net loss of $(2.0) million, compared with net income of $1.5 million; non-GAAP net income of $34.3 million, up 269 percent GAAP EPS (diluted) of $(0.03); non-GAAP EPS (diluted) of $0.60 Adjusted EBITDA of $70.1 million, up 202 percent; Adjusted EBITDA margin of 17.3% Free cash flow of $148.4 million, a $137.3 million improvement; adjusted free cash flow of $154.4 million, a $135.4 million improvement, adjusted for cash payments relating to the Thermon transaction made during the quarter Leverage of 2.0X, a reduction of 0.7X from the closing date of the Thermon acquisition (1) All comparisons are versus the comparable prior year period, unless otherwise stated. Reconciliations of GAAP (reported) to non-GAAP measures are in the attached financial tables. Todd Gleason, CECO's Chairman and Chief Executive Officer commented: “Our strong third quarter results reflect CECO’s leadership in attractive and growing niche markets across a range of resilient industrial end markets. Customers around the world rely on our solutions and expertise to meet or exceed critical environmental and process safety requirements. Our sustainable growth is a testament to the strength of our incredible portfolio, the dedication of our employees, and the support of our global partners. We have a proven track record of creating value for our customers, partners, communities and our shareholders. While recent headlines and U.S. election developments have created volatility in equity markets, which we certainly monitor, we remain focused on the factors within our control. The continued visibility we have in our $2.2 billion backlog – the vast majority of which is permitted and underway, our rapidly growing $9 billion sales pipeline, and our productivity and synergy initiatives reinforce my confidence in our strategy and my conviction in our ability to deliver significant long-term value creation.” Third quarter operating income was $10.5 million, compared with operating income of $9.4 million in the prior-year quarter. On an adjusted basis, non-GAAP operating income was $55.7 million, up $38.2 million or 218 percent compared with $17.5 million in the prior-year quarter. Net loss was $(2.0) million in the quarter, compared with net income of $1.5 million in the prior-year quarter. Non-GAAP net income was $34.3 million, an increase of $25.0 million, or 269 percent, from $9.3 million in the prior-year quarter. Adjusted EBITDA was $70.1 million, reflecting a margin of 17.3 percent, an increase of $46.9 million, or 202 percent, compared with $23.2 million in the prior-year quarter. Adjusted free cash flow in the quarter was $154.4 million, an improvement of $135.4 million compared with $19.0 million in the prior-year quarter. “Since closing the Thermon acquisition in June, we have substantially completed key integration initiatives. We remain ahead of schedule on both our cost and revenue synergies, and the combination is an excellent cultural fit. Across our entire CECO portfolio, we continue to see strong momentum driven by growth across our diverse end markets, increasing customer demand, and the continued execution of our operational initiatives, which are contributing to margin expansion and enhanced cash flow generation. Our proven operating model has delivered regular double-digit growth and meaningful margin expansion since 2021, and I expect will continue to drive strong performance in 2027 and 2028. While we are pleased to have delivered more than 100 percent revenue growth and over 200 percent growth in orders, backlog and Adjusted EBITDA during the third quarter, we are even more excited about the future. The strategic investments we have made to strengthen and expand our industrial leadership into new markets position us to drive even higher levels of performance in the years to come,” added Gleason. 2026 Full Year Guidance Update The Company is updating its full-year 2026 outlook as a result of the strong year-to-date performance and near-term market opportunities. The updated full year consolidated 2026 outlook is: Raising full year Orders to exceed $2.5 billion, compared to previous outlook of at least $2.0 billion Raising full year free cash flow conversion to approximately 100 percent of Adjusted EBITDA, compared to previous outlook of at least 55 percent Maintaining full year Revenue outlook of between $1.300 billion and $1.375 billion Maintaining full year Adjusted EBITDA outlook of between $200 million and $225 million “As we work to conclude another banner year at CECO, we expect to deliver results at or above the full year guidance we have raised multiple times throughout the year, including the most recent increase in August. The projects in our backlog remain largely on schedule, and our sales pipeline continues to expand in both size and quantity. While we anticipate additional orders to be realized in power markets, I would emphasize that demand for our environmental, industrial and thermal solutions remain equally robust and often are realized later in the project supply chain cycle and generally represent funded, active projects rather than speculative demand,” added Gleason. Introducing 2027 Full Year Outlook The Company introduces its 2027 full year outlook with revenue expected to be between $2.1 billion and $2.3 billion, representing growth of more than 60 percent at the midpoint compared with the midpoint of the Company’s 2026 revenue outlook, and Adjusted EBITDA between $475 million and $525 million, representing growth of more than 130 percent at the midpoint compared with the midpoint of the Company’s 2026 Adjusted EBITDA outlook. The Company expects full year free cash flow of between 50 percent and 60 percent of Adjusted EBITDA. Mr. Gleason concluded, “CECO continues to transform and drive high-performance thanks to our incredible teams executing at high levels and generating incredible returns on our growth and operating improvement investments. Our full year 2027 outlook highlights further growth and scale. Since introducing our annual guidance process back in Q3 2021, we have a solid track record of meeting or exceeding our outlook as we incorporate significant backlog and pipeline insights, conservative assumptions on inflation and key market dynamics. The combination of our proven process and consistent track record, along with our visibility into our backlog and sales pipeline, gives us high confidence that 2027 will be another rewarding year for all our stakeholders.” EARNINGS CONFERENCE CALL A conference call is scheduled for today at 8:30 a.m. ET to discuss the third quarter 2026 financial results. Please visit the Investor Relations section of the website (https://investors.cecoenviro.com) to listen to the call via webcast. The conference call may also be accessed by visiting https://edge.media-server.com/mmc/p/x4b7b8us. A replay of the conference call will be available on the Company’s website for a period of one year. The replay may also be accessed by visiting https://investors.cecoenviro.com/. ABOUT CECO ENVIRONMENTAL CECO Environmental is a leading environmentally focused, diversified industrial company, serving the broad landscape of industrial air, industrial water and energy transition markets globally providing innovative solutions and application expertise. CECO helps companies grow their businesses with safe, clean, and more efficient solutions that help protect people, the environment and industrial equipment. CECO solutions improve air and water quality, optimize emissions management, and increase energy efficiency for highly-engineered applications in power generation, midstream and downstream hydrocarbon processing and transport, electric vehicle production, polysilicon fabrication, semiconductor and electronics, battery production and recycling, specialty metals and steel production, beverage can production, and water/wastewater treatment and a wide range of other industrial end markets. articles.summary: By Fabrizio Sardo, Vice President of Operations To understand what it takes to manufacture a rugged computing system, it helps to start with something unlikely to appear in a product brochure: a thermal pad. On a drawing, the pad has a precise location; at the workbench, meeting that requirement involves cutting material, positioning it accurately, and assembling the surrounding components. During OSS assembly and cycle-time reviews, these routine tasks prompted questions about whether a cutting fixture or alignment guide might improve consistency, as well as how connector seating, tool access, and test sequencing could influence the build. Such details rarely appear in a product specification, yet they help determine whether instructions are clear, work is repeatable, and each person has what they need to do the job correctly. Our customers are understandably focused on performance, from processing and storage to cooling and operation outside the conventional data center, but delivering that capability requires coordination among Engineering, Operations, Quality, and the people who assemble and test OSS systems. The Work Starts Before the Workbench A production date on the schedule does not always mean an order is ready to build. Beyond material availability, planners must consider remaining work, assembly and test capacity, and repair activity that draws on the same people and equipment; Procurement must also account for supplier processes that affect when a part is ready for assembly. Consider a circuit board requiring conformal coating. Sending it to a processor is only one step, because the drawing must communicate coating and masking requirements, while Procurement, Engineering, and Quality need a shared understanding of the expected result before the board reaches assembly. That preparation is easy to overlook, but it helps make the production schedule credible. Rather than asking only whether an order is open or materials have arrived, our planning discussions focus on what must be true before the next operation begins, bringing materials, documentation, and floor capacity into the same conversation. Where Engineering Intent Meets Manufacturing Reality A drawing establishes what must be built, but it cannot capture everything an assembler encounters at the workbench. It may show exactly where a component belongs without revealing how easily someone can reach a fastener, handle a cable, or fully seat a connector, questions the people doing the work are often the first to raise. I see that feedback as an essential part of disciplined manufacturing, rather than a complaint to dismiss or permission to make unapproved changes. When questions reach the right technical owner and the resolution is reflected in the build information, everyone can work from the same approved understanding. Manufacturing engineering helps turn those observations into practical improvement opportunities by studying builds, cycle times, and tooling to identify ways to make work more consistent. Our thermal-pad review generated ideas such as a cutting fixture or alignment guide, but an idea must be evaluated before it becomes standard practice; proposing an improvement and demonstrating its value are not the same thing. The goal is a process people can understand, execute, and repeat without compromising the design. What It Takes to Call a System Ready A system may look complete when assembly ends, but readiness for delivery depends on more than its appearance. Depending on the configuration, setup and acceptance testing still must follow the applicable procedure, making test equipment, technician availability, and engineering support as important to scheduling as assembly capacity. When a test result needs investigation, Test, Engineering, Production, and Quality may each hold part of the answer. At the same time, the hardware configuration, applicable procedure, and recorded results must remain aligned; without that traceability, we cannot reliably establish what was tested and what was verified. Even a system that has passed testing may not be ready to ship, because packaging, release documentation, and customer-specific conditions still require attention. There are times when a shipment should be held while a requirement or document is clarified, and those decisions deserve the same care as earlier technical work. By the time a customer sees the completed system, the questions raised at the bench, the supplier requirements clarified upstream, and the test and release records reviewed are largely invisible. Although different teams make these decisions at different points, their combined judgment shapes what ultimately leaves our facility. I do not view Operations as the department that takes over once Engineering completes a design; our role is to help turn engineering intent into hardware that can be built consistently, tested appropriately, documented accurately, and delivered to the customer. That work depends on people throughout OSS whose contributions may never appear in a product launch, but whose judgment affects every build. Specifications describe what an OSS system is designed to do; the work behind the build is how we make that design ready to deliver. If you are developing a rugged edge computing application, connect with OSS to discuss its requirements and the practical work involved in taking it from design to delivery.
articles.title: Behind the Build: From Design to Delivery at OSS

articles.summary: Bain Capital Specialty Finance Appoints Amrit Kanwal to its Board of Directors bcsf_admin Mon, 11/09/2026 - 16:54 Body Boston--Bain Capital Specialty Finance, Inc. (“BCSF” or the “Company”) (NYSE: BCSF) today announced the appointment of Amrit Kanwal as an independent director to its Board of Directors (the “Board”), effective November 4, 2026. Mr. Kanwal will serve on the Audit, Nominating and Corporate Governance, and Compensation Committees. BCSF’s Board now includes nine members, including six independent directors. Mr. Kanwal is an accomplished C-suite executive leader and board director with extensive financial and strategic expertise across financial services, mutual funds, and consumer goods. Effective November 4, 2026, Mr. Kanwal was also appointed as an independent director of Bain Capital Private Credit, a non-traded business development company that is externally managed by an affiliate of BCSF Advisors, LP, the Company’s investment adviser and a subsidiary of Bain Capital Credit, LP. Mr. Kanwal currently serves as an independent director for Columbia Threadneedle Investments and as a director of the Arete Newbury Fund. Mr. Kanwal previously held board positions at MFS Investment Management, Aditya Birla Sun Life Asset Management, Meridian Funds, PanAgora Asset Management, among others. Over a 16-year tenure as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of MFS Investment Management, he drove global expansion and grew enterprise earnings more than sixfold. Previously, Mr. Kanwal served as Chief Financial Officer of Putnam Investments, where he successfully led corporate turnaround and stabilization strategies, ultimately orchestrating the firm's sale to Great-West Lifeco Inc. in 2007. “As a proven executive leader and global strategist, Amrit will further bolster our Board’s capabilities and composition, and we welcome him to BCSF,” said Michael Ewald, Chief Executive Officer of BCSF. “His breadth of expertise in finance, treasury, and strategy and deep governance background will be a valuable resource to the Board as we continue to deliver shareholder value.” “I have long admired Bain Capital as a firm for its partnership approach and the rigor and discipline they bring to investing,” said Mr. Kanwal. “I am proud to join BCSF’s Board and look forward to collaborating closely with my fellow directors to continue to drive the Company’s long-term success.” Earlier in his career, Mr. Kanwal worked in corporate development and finance roles at Miller Brewing, Pepsi-Cola, and Sequa Corporation. He holds a Bachelor of Business Administration degree from the University of Texas at Austin and a Master of Business Administration degree from the University of Southern California's Marshall School of Business. Mr. Kanwal is actively involved in youth development and sports philanthropy, currently serving on the board of the US Squash Foundation. About Bain Capital Specialty Finance, Inc. Bain Capital Specialty Finance, Inc. is an externally managed specialty finance company focused on lending to middle market companies. BCSF is managed by BCSF Advisors, LP, an SEC-registered investment adviser and a subsidiary of Bain Capital Credit, LP. Since commencing investment operations on October 13, 2016, and through September 30, 2026, BCSF has invested approximately $10,238.4 million in aggregate principal amount of debt and equity investments prior to any subsequent exits or repayments. BCSF’s investment objective is to generate current income and, to a lesser extent, capital appreciation through direct originations of secured debt, including first lien, first lien/last out, unitranche and second lien debt, investments in strategic joint ventures, equity investments and, to a lesser extent, corporate bonds. BCSF has elected to be regulated as a business development company under the Investment Company Act of 1940, as amended.
